This study focuses on predicting video frames from novel viewpoints, a challenge particularly difficult for deep learning models due to the lack of corresponding viewpoint frames in typical video datasets like Sports 1M and also Rogue Wave in maritime environments. To address this issue, we propose an innovative video forecasting model that can handle novel viewpoints, even if no corresponding frames exist. The proposed model consists of two components: a view-aware transformer encoder that generates frames from novel viewpoints and a view-aware transformer decoder that refines these generated frames. One key feature of this model is the use of view representation learning, which enables the model to effectively handle novel viewpoints by learning the distinct features of frames from various viewpoints in the available datasets like Sports 1M and Rogue Wave. Another key feature is the use of a view embedding matrix to incorporate viewpoint information into the frame generation process. To further improve the model's performance, we propose an innovative view representation learning approach that combines view-aware contrastive learning with view-aware similarity metrics. One view similarity metric used in this approach is the viewpoint angle difference, the other is the viewpoint change frequency. The proposed model achieves the best performance compared to existing models like TOG, TOG+, TOG-FP, and TOG-FC in typical video datasets like Sports 1M and Rogue Wave, indicating its potential applications in various fields like maritime safety, sports analysis, and entertainment. The proposed model also outperforms existing models like TOG, TOG+, TOG-FP, and TOG-FC in subjective quality assessments, further confirming its effectiveness. The proposed model's ability to handle novel viewpoints makes it an attractive option for researchers and developers in various fields like computer vision, electronics, and communications engineering.
